Q #9 Multiple Choice Type Award: 1 Penalty: 0.33 Databases Medium (59%)

Codd's rule of physical data independence is that

  1. all information in the database is to be represented in one and only one way, namely by values in column positions within rows of tables.
  2. all views that are theoretically updatable must be updatable by the system.
  3. changes that are made to the physical storage representations or access methods must not require changes be made to application programs.
  4. changes that are made to tables that do not modify any of the data already stored in the tables must not require changes be made to application programs.

Q #18 Multiple Select Type Award: 2 Penalty: 0 Databases Medium (31%)

Two more exotic relational algebra operators are the semijoin (⋉) ( ⋉ ) and antijoin (▹) ( ▹ ) . Semijoin is the same as natural join, except only attributes of the first relation are returned in the result. For example, if we have relations Student(ID, name) Student(ID, name) and Enrolled(ID, course), Enrolled(ID, course) , and not all students are enrolled in courses, then the query "Student ⋉ ⋉ Enrolled" returns the ID and name of all students who are enrolled in at least one course. In the general case, E1⋉E2 E 1 ⋉ E 2 returns all tuples in the result of expression E1 E 1 such that there is at least one tuple in the result of E2 E 2 with matching values for the shared attributes. antijoin is the converse: E1▹E2 E 1 ▹ E 2 returns all tuples in the result of expression E1 E 1 such that there are no tuples in the result of E2 E 2 with matching values for the shared attributes. For example, the query "Student ▹ ▹ Enrolled" returns the ID and name of all students who are not enrolled in any courses.

  1. E1⋉E2=πschema(E1)(E1⋈E2) E 1 ⋉ E 2 = π schema ⁡ ( E 1 ) ( E 1 ⋈ E 2 )
     
  2. E1▹E2=E1−πschema(E1)(E1⋈E2) E 1 ▹ E 2 = E 1 − π schema ⁡ ( E 1 ) ( E 1 ⋈ E 2 )
     
  3. (E1▹E2)∪(E1⋉E2)=E1 ( E 1 ▹ E 2 ) ∪ ( E 1 ⋉ E 2 ) = E 1
     
  4. (E1▹E2)⋈(E1⋉E2)=E1 ( E 1 ▹ E 2 ) ⋈ ( E 1 ⋉ E 2 ) = E 1
